t:
Section 16(b) of the Act entitled “An Act to establish the National Bureau of Standards”, approved March 3, 1901 (15 U.S.C. 278Kb)), is amended to read as follows:


“(b) 
Authorization of Appropriations.—For purposes of this section, there are authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $5,650,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, which amount includes—

“(1) 
$525,000 for programs which are recommended in the report submitted to the Congress by the Administrator of the United States Fire Administration pursuant to section 24(b)(1) of the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2220(b)(1)); and


“(2) 
$119,000 for adjustments required by law in salaries, pay, retirement, and employee benefits.”.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations for a fiscal year. The tempting reading is that "recommended in the report submitted to the Congress" signals consultation, but that report goes from a federal official to Congress, both inside the federal government. No outside party (states, the public, experts, industry) is consulted or given a role in any federal decision.
fable.s: $525,000 for programs which are recommended in the report submitted to the Congress by the Administrator of the United States Fire Administration

opus.w: This section only authorizes funding amounts. The one procedural reference is a report from a federal official (the Fire Administrator) to Congress, and both are inside the federal government. No states, experts, members of the public, or other outside parties are consulted, so this is not participation.
opus.s: $525,000 for programs which are recommended in the report submitted to the Congress by the Administrator of the United States Fire Administration

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations based on a report submitted to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and reports to Congress are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. The text does not describe any consultation with or coordination by outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. It is purely an internal funding authorization linked to an internal report.
qwen_chat.s: $525,000 for programs which are recommended in the report submitted to the Congress by the Administrator of the United States Fire Administration pursuant to section 24(b)(1) of the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2220(b)(1))
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funding is tied to a report submitted to Congress, and Congress is part of the government, this is just internal reporting. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "No" because Congress is inside the federal government. The section itself does not describe any process where the federal government consults with outsiders (like the public, states, or private entities) before making a decision. It merely authorizes funding based on a report that was already submitted. There is no mechanism for outside participation described in this text.
